Deformation at temperatures and strain rates between 1040°C to 1140°C and 0.1/s to 0.001/s resulted in a transition of dominant deformation mechanisms from dislocation based plasticity to grain boundary rotation and sliding.

Two distinct forms of damage were observed: cavitation damage and interfacial debonding of the δ phase precipitates.
Plastic deformation was observed above the transition stress while creep deformation was predominant during deformation involving stresses below the transition stress.
flow stresses were significantly reduced as grain boundary sliding and rotation were dominant.
